newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end weaker, but above day's lows.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end weaker, but above day's lows.

text.p: Mexico's stock market picked up strength during the day after tumbling more than 2 percent to close closer to 1 percent down Friday.
The market's main index ended down 0.882 percent, or 29.43 points, at 3,305.47 points.
The market had a bad case of nerves Friday, compounded by the weakness on Wall Street and widespread guerrilla attacks earlier in the week in Mexico.

"There were a lot of things that affected the Mexican market. People were selling because of guerrillas, the increase in the long bond, and nervousness before the president's state of the union address," said one brokerage house dealer.
President Ernesto Zedillo will give his annual state of the union address Sunday.

At midday, the market had shed 2.0 percent, but then climbed back up, cushioned by end-of-month buying and an easing of the decline in the Dow Jones average. Brokers said they noticed some foreign buyers entering the market again.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 31.44 points at 5,616.21 points.

Interacciones technical analyst Jaime Fernandez said that it was important that Mexico's main index respected the support level of 3,270 points, and that this indicated an upward trend in the medium term.
Among the biggest decliners was Grupo Financiero Abaco series B, which shed 30 centavos (four cents) to 2.50 pesos (33 cents).
Among the winners was Sidek A, which rose 16 centavos (2 cents) to 1.83 pesos (24 cents).
Volume was 97,053,706. There were 24 gainers, 50 decliners, and 19 unchanged.
